title: History and Founder
subtitle: Our roots and our continuing story
intro: Vunimono High School’s story is grounded in a long commitment to education and community.

sections.title: Our Beginnings
sections.text: The history of Vunimono High School is rooted in the vision, sacrifices and dedication of the pioneers of the Sanatan Dharam Mahamandal (Vunimono), Fiji. Their commitment to education, community development and service laid the foundation for an institution that continues to provide educational opportunities to students in the Suva–Nausori corridor and beyond. The Mahamandal’s educational mission can be traced to the work of Sadhu Girwar Dass Mahant, a Hindu priest, indentured labourer and visionary educationist from India, whose life and work inspired the school’s values.

sections.title: The Establishment of Vunimono High School in 1972
sections.text: By 1971, the Sanatan Dharam Mahamandal recognised an urgent need for a secondary school in Vunimono. The limited number of secondary schools in the Nausori area could not accommodate the increasing number of primary school leavers seeking further education, and students who sought places in Suva faced intense competition and long travel distances. In response, the Mahamandal established Vunimono High School in 1972, beginning with just 34 students in one form and operating under the leadership of Mr S. N. Hari Prasad.

sections.title: Overcoming Challenges and Building for the Future
sections.text: The early years were marked by determination, sacrifice and collective effort. The management faced significant challenges in recruiting qualified teachers and securing the financial resources needed to operate and expand the school. Through community fundraising, donations, loans and support from parents, teachers and students, the school continued to grow and serve the needs of the local community.

sections.title: A Period of Rapid Growth: 1973–1979
sections.text: Under the leadership of Mr R. S. Yadav, the school expanded quickly, with enrolment rising from 330 students in 1973 to 830 by 1977. New classrooms, science laboratories and temporary structures were added, and the school began offering the Fiji Junior Certificate and upper secondary education opportunities. The community’s commitment and the Mahamandal’s support were central to this period of growth and development.

sections.title: Expanding Educational Opportunities
sections.text: In 1982, the school introduced Industrial Arts and Home Economics, broadening the curriculum and helping students develop practical skills alongside academic learning. This reflected the school’s growing commitment to holistic education, ensuring that students were prepared not only for examinations but also for life, work and responsible citizenship.

sections.title: Infrastructure Development and Modernisation
sections.text: From 2006 onward, significant infrastructure improvements strengthened the school environment. The Government of Japan, through JICA support, helped construct additional classrooms, while the Mahamandal continued upgrading the administration block, staff facilities, library, department rooms and safety features. These developments ensured a more modern, secure and supportive learning environment for students and staff.

sections.title: Academic Excellence and Holistic Education
sections.text: Vunimono High School recognises that education extends beyond the classroom. Students are encouraged to excel in academic competitions, leadership activities, cultural events and sporting programmes, while the school continues to invest in textbooks, learning resources and facilities that support improved educational outcomes and student growth.

sections.title: Leadership Through the Years
sections.text: The development of the school has been guided by successive leaders, including Bijen Singh, whose service reflects the wider commitment of principals, teachers, ancillary staff, parents and the Mahamandal Board to building a strong school community. Their collective efforts have shaped the school’s growth and continued relevance in the district.

sections.title: Our Legacy and the Road Ahead
sections.text: From just 34 students in 1972, Vunimono High School has grown into a respected institution serving families across the Suva–Nausori corridor and beyond. Its history is a story of vision, partnership and service, and the school continues to build on these values as it looks to a future of growth, achievement, unity and community responsibility.
